documents.t: Some warnings (e.g. a DOM operation that matches nothing) are logged only when __DEV__ is defined and truthy. In webpack define it with DefinePlugin, in Vite with define: vite.config.js export default defineConfig({ define: { __DEV__: JSON.stringify(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') } });

A module is a default export: a function, a class or an object. resources/js/MyModule.js export default class MyModule { init(...args) { console.log('Hello world!', args); } } Call it from the server: $response = new \dobron\BigPipe\AsyncResponse(); $response->call('MyModule', 'init', [ 'first argument', 'second argument', ]); $response->send();
Make links and forms asynchronous with the Primer. Send requests from your code with AsyncRequest. Learn what the server sends back in How it works.

BigPipe moves the decision about what happens on the page to the server. The browser only sends a request, the server answers with a list of instructions and bigpipe-util executes them. The user clicks a link or submits a form handled by the Primer, or your code sends an AsyncRequest. The server responds with DOM operations (domops) and JavaScript modules to call (jsmods). AsyncResponse applies the DOM operations, then ServerJS loads and calls the modules.

A response is JSON prefixed with the for (;;); shield. The shield makes the response unusable when it's loaded with a <script> tag from another site; AsyncRequest strips it before parsing. The server sends it as application/json with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so the browser never runs it as a script either. for (;;);{"payload":null,"domops":[...],"jsmods":{"require":[...]},"__ar":1} Key Description payload Custom data for your handler, see setPayload() on the server. domops DOM operations, applied in order. pagelets Optional pagelets, handed to BigPipe after the DOM operations, e.g. a pagelet loaded lazily or refreshed. jsmods Modules to call, see ServerJS. revision Optional revision of the deploy of the server, see a new deploy. resource_map Optional names of CSS and JS files, see the Bootloader. bootloadable Optional files of modules loaded on demand, see bootloadable modules. __ar Marks the response as an async response. AsyncResponse reads the revision first, then resource_map and bootloadable, applies the DOM operations, hands the pagelets to BigPipe and calls the modules last. AsyncRequest reads a few more keys. csrf_refresh sends the request again, once, with a new CSRF token. error, errorSummary, errorDescription, errorIsWarning and isTransient describe an error the server sent. The whole response object is also passed to the handler set with setHandler().

A streamed response is a series of parts, each followed by the delimiter /*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/. A part is JSON with a response as content and finished on the last part: {"content":{"payload":{"title":"Feed"},"domops":[...],"jsmods":{"define":[...]}},"finished":false}/*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/ {"content":{"pagelets":[{"id":"feed",...}]},"finished":false}/*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/ {"content":{"pagelets":[{"id":"__bigpipe_last","is_last":true,...}],"jsmods":{"require":[...]}},"finished":true}/*<!-- fetch-stream -->*/

Each operation is an array [type, selector, targetRelative, content]: ["appendContent", "ul.logs", false, {"__html": "
  • appended line
    • "}] type: one of setContent, appendContent, prependContent, insertAfter, insertBefore, replace, morph, morphContent (see morphing), remove, hide, show and eval (deprecated: a Content Security Policy without 'unsafe-eval' blocks it, call a module with jsmods instead). selector: a CSS selector of the element to change. targetRelative: when true, the operation targets the element that sent the request (the clicked link or the submitted form), or the element matching selector inside it. The PHP library sets it when the selector is empty. content: HTML wrapped in the __html transport marker, or JavaScript code for eval, which runs with this bound to the element. The content of a pagelet of the page may be {"__container": "u_0_5"} instead, the id of a hidden element the page printed before the script of the pagelet, with the HTML in a comment, where \ and - are escaped with a backslash (see BigPipe::setHtmlContainers() in the PHP library). The HTML is then not escaped in the JSON of the script, and the browser does not parse it until the pagelet is displayed. The container is removed. Operations whose selector matches nothing are skipped. With __DEV__ defined and truthy (see Getting started), an error is logged to the console.

AsyncRequest hands every successful response to AsyncResponse. You can use it directly to process a response you received in another way, e.g. over a WebSocket: import AsyncResponse from 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncResponse'; socket.addEventListener('message', ({ data }) => { new AsyncResponse().handle(JSON.parse(data)); });

Layer is the base of everything that floats above the page: a menu, a tooltip, a dialog. It shows and hides a DOM element, tells what happens through events, and gets its behaviour from behaviors that you enable per layer. It does not depend on a CSS framework: it sets no class names and only the inline styles it needs to work, so the element can be styled with Bootstrap, Tailwind or your own CSS. import Layer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/Layer'; const layer = new Layer('
Menu
', { classNames: ['shadow-lg'], // added to the root, with any classes of your own attributes: { role: 'menu' }, causalElement: button, // what opened it insertParent: document.body, // where the root is put when it's shown, the body by default behaviors: [HideOnEscape] }); layer.show(); layer.hide(); layer.destroy(); // removes the root and disables the behaviors The first argument is a DOM element or an HTML string with a single root element. A root that is hidden is hidden with display: none while the layer is not shown.

Subscribe with layer.subscribe(name, callback), or an array of names. The callback gets the data of the event and the name of the event, and remove() of the returned subscription unsubscribes. A callback that returns false stops what the event is about, where it says so. Event When beforeshow The layer is about to be shown. show It is shown. aftershow It is shown and positioned. beforehide hide() was called, with the source. Returning false keeps the layer open. starthide The layer starts to hide. Returning false postpones it: call finishHide() when ready, e.g. after a fade. hide It is hidden. destroy It is destroyed. key A key was pressed while it is open, with the KeyboardEvent, topmost layer first. Returning false handles the key: its default action is prevented and it does not reach the layers below or the page. Keys typed in a text field are not informed, except for keys like Esc in an empty one, and Tab. blur The user clicked outside of the layer, with { target }. Returning false stops it from reaching the layers below. Layer.subscribe(name, callback) listens to show, hide and destroy of all layers, with the layer as the data. Layer.getTopmostLayer() is the layer that was shown last, Layer.getLayerOf(element) the layer of a root, Layer.getLayerContaining(element) the innermost layer an element is in, and Layer.containsIncludingLayers(root, element) tells whether an element is inside of root or of a layer opened from inside of it, at any depth. A click counts as a click outside only when the mouse was pressed and released on the same element outside of the layer and of the layers opened from inside it (their causalElement, or the context of a ContextualLayer, is inside it), at any depth.

A behavior is a class with a constructor that gets the layer, and enable() and disable(). Pass them in behaviors, or use layer.enableBehaviors([...]) and layer.disableBehaviors([...]). Every behavior is enabled once per layer. class LogOnShow { constructor(layer) { this.layer = layer; } enable() { this.subscription = this.layer.subscribe('show', () => console.log('shown')); } disable() { this.subscription.remove(); } }

The hide() of a layer takes the source of the request, one of HideSources (blur, escape, success, transition), which beforehide and starthide get as their data. Behavior Does HideOnEscape Hides the topmost layer when Esc is pressed, and handles the key. HideOnBlur Hides the layer on a click outside of it. Layers below stay open. HideOnTransition Hides the layer before a page transition. Override isTransitionRelevant({ from, to }) to hide only for some. HideOnSuccess Hides the layer when a request sent from inside of it succeeds, see the success event. The hideOnSuccess option of the layer is true for any request, or a selector of the elements that sent it. DestroyOnHide Destroys the layer after it was hidden. RemoveOnHide Removes the root from the page when the layer is hidden. show() puts it back. import Layer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/Layer'; import HideOnBlur from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/HideOnBlur'; import HideOnEscape from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/HideOnEscape'; new Layer(menuElement, { behaviors: [HideOnBlur, HideOnEscape] }).show();

Behavior Does AutoFocus Moves the focus into the layer when it is shown: to the element with autofocus, else the first control (not a link), else the root. A control inside that already has the focus keeps it. TabIsolation Keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside of the layer, also under layers that don't, when it is the last one shown with TabIsolation. In a layer opened from inside of it, e.g. a menu in the body, Tab moves through that layer and from its ends back to the element that opened it. RefocusOnHide Gives the focus back to the causalElement, or else the element that had it before the layer was shown, when the focus was in the layer. When that element is hidden by now, the focus goes to the closest visible element instead: the opener of the hidden layer it is in, or an ancestor, which gets tabindex="-1" to take the focus. focusWithinLayer(element) from core/layer/focusWithinLayer is the focus logic of AutoFocus, and getTabbable(element) lists the elements Tab reaches: not disabled, not hidden (hidden, display: none) and visible.

FadeOnShow and FadeOnHide fade the root with an inline opacity transition, so they work with any CSS. They take 100 and 150 ms, and FadeOnShow.forDuration(300) and FadeOnHide.forDuration(300) return behaviors with another duration. Users who prefer reduced motion get no animation. FadeOnHide postpones the hiding with starthide and calls finishHide() when the fade is over.

ModalLayer makes a layer modal: it puts a backdrop before the root, locks the scrolling of the page, centers the root and stacks modals so that the last one shown is on top, with the only visible backdrop. Modals and dialogs share one stacking order, so a modal opened from a dialog is above it, and the other way round. Combine it with HideOnBlur to hide on a click on the backdrop and HideOnEscape for Esc. import ModalLayer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/ModalLayer'; new Layer(dialogElement, { behaviors: [ModalLayer, HideOnBlur, HideOnEscape, AutoFocus, TabIsolation] }).show(); It styles the backdrop and centers the root with inline styles, so it works without any CSS. To use your own, ModalLayer.configure() returns a behavior with other options: const Modal = ModalLayer.configure({ backdropClassName: 'fixed inset-0 bg-black/50', // no default look is applied when set backdropStyle: { backdropFilter: 'blur(2px)' }, zIndex: 50, // of the backdrop, the root is 1 above; a modal shown // over another one is at least 10 above it center: false, // position the root with your CSS lockScroll: false }); With center: false the root has to be positioned (e.g. fixed) by your CSS for the z-index to apply.

ContextualLayer is a Layer that is positioned next to an element, for menus, tooltips and popovers. It is placed with position: absolute in the page, or in its insertParent when that is (or is inside of) a positioned or transformed element. import ContextualLayer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/ContextualLayer'; const menu = new ContextualLayer(menuElement, { context: button, // an element, or a function that returns one position: 'below', // above, below, left or right alignment: 'start', // start, center or end of the context offsetX: 0, offsetY: 4, autoFlip: true, // the other side when it doesn't fit in the viewport keepInViewport: true, behaviors: [HideOnBlur, HideOnEscape] }); menu.show(); menu.getPosition(); // the side it was placed on after flipping menu.setPosition('right'); It is positioned again while it is shown when the window is resized or scrolled and informs reposition with the side and alignment. A layer whose context is inside of another layer, e.g. a submenu, is hidden with that layer, and its context is its causalElement unless one is set. A layer whose context is not on the page or not displayed (display: none) is not shown. When the context is inside of a modal or a dialog (a positioned ancestor with a z-index), the layer gets a z-index 1 above it.

Tooltip shows one tooltip for the whole page, a ContextualLayer next to an element while the pointer is over it or it has the focus. Set the tooltip of an element once: import Tooltip from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Tooltip'; Tooltip.set(button, 'Saves the draft'); Tooltip.set(avatar, 'Loading…', { uri: '/ajax/hovercard?id=4', position: 'below' }); Tooltip.set(title, null, { overflow: true }); The content is text, where new lines are kept, a DOM node or {__html}. The options: Option Does position above (default), below, left or right. It flips to the other side when it doesn't fit. alignment start, center (default) or end of the element. delay Milliseconds the pointer has to stay before it is shown. className Added to the tooltip while it shows this content. persistOnClick Stays shown on a click on the element, which hides it otherwise. overflow Shown only when the text of the element is cut off, e.g. with text-overflow: ellipsis, and with that text when there is no content. uri Loads the content once, on the first hover, from the payload of a response ($response->setPayload()), showing the content until then. It hides when the pointer or the focus leaves the element, on Esc, on scroll and before a page transition. While it is shown, the element is aria-describedby the tooltip, whose role is tooltip. Tooltip.show(element), Tooltip.hide(), Tooltip.remove(element) and Tooltip.isActive(element) control it from code, and Tooltip.getLayer() is its layer. It has a dark inline look, so it works without CSS. Tooltip.configure({ className: 'tooltip', zIndex: 60, delay: 300 }) replaces the look with your class, puts it above your other layers and sets the default delay. The server sets tooltips with a call, e.g. for an element of a pagelet: $pagelet->call('bigpipe-util/dist/core/Tooltip', 'set', [ TransportMarker::element('save-button'), 'Saves the draft', ['position' => 'below'], ]);

Dialogs are layers: DialogLayer wraps a Modal, keeps its events and markup, and adds the layer events and behaviors (AutoFocus, TabIsolation, RefocusOnHide, HideOnTransition, and HideOnSuccess which hides the layer when a request sent from inside succeeds, see the success event). A dialog is always shown through the modal, so it does not use ModalLayer and the fades, which the modal has built in.

With bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry, the layers and the behaviors are modules the server can require, e.g. a menu the server keeps as an instance and shows later: use dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker; $menu = $response->instance('bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/ContextualLayer', [ '
…
', [ 'context' => TransportMarker::element('menu-button'), 'behaviors' => [ TransportMarker::module('bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/HideOnBlur'), TransportMarker::module('bigpipe-util/dist/core/layer/HideOnEscape'), ], ], ]); $menu->call('show'); calculateTopMargin(height, options) from core/layer/DialogPosition is the top margin of a dialog for the position option: options.top when it is set, else a third of the free height of the window (half with centered), at least 40.

With page transitions, the links of the site load the next page into the element with the content of the page, the canvas, instead of loading the page in full. The header, the scripts and everything the page has loaded stay, so only the content of the next page and its pagelets are requested and rendered. The server turns them on for a page by calling Quickling.init() with the canvas, see Quickling in the PHP library: Quickling.init(document.getElementById('content'), { version: '2026-10-10', // a page of another version is loaded in full inactivePageRegex: '^/admin', // paths always loaded in full badRequestKeys: ['print'], // query parameters that need a full load sessionLength: 50 // after this many page transitions the next page is loaded in full });

PageTransitions takes over the clicks on the links of the page and the GET forms. A link is left to the browser when it goes to another origin, opens a new window (target), is a download, is handled by the Primer (rel="async", rel="dialog", ajaxify), has rel="external", or is clicked with a modifier key or another button than the main one. A link to a fragment of the current page only scrolls to it, and a link to an empty fragment of it, like href="#", does nothing. PageTransitions.go(url) loads a page from JavaScript; PageTransitions.go(url, true) replaces the current history entry instead of adding one, as a redirect of the server does. The back and forward buttons load the page of the history entry and restore its scroll position, also for the entries other scripts added with history.pushState(); an entry of the same page with another fragment only scrolls to it. Every entry keeps its own scroll position, also in its history.state, so it is restored after a reload too. When a page transition can't be used, the page is loaded in full: when the page must not be handled, the request fails, or the server sends a page of another version, e.g. after a deploy.

Quickling requests the URL with GET and the parameter quickling[version]. The server responds with an AsyncResponse whose payload has: version: the version of the page, compared with the one of Quickling.init(). title: the title of the page, the title is kept without one. body_class: the class of <body>, the class is kept without one. redirect: a URL to go to instead, with a page transition, or in full with force. Before the response is applied, the pagelets in the canvas are destroyed, Pagelet/destroy is informed with the canvas as root, and the canvas is emptied. Its DOM operations then fill the canvas (the element the request is relative to) and its pagelets are loaded like on a page. Only the response of the latest page transition is applied. The request is streamed: a server that sends every pagelet as soon as it is rendered shows the next page progressively, like a page streamed with BigPipe::stream(). The page transition completes once the pagelets of the last part are displayed.

The page keeps the scripts it was loaded with. When the server defines the revision of its deploy as the BigPipeRevision module (BigPipe::setRevision() in the PHP library), every response carries the revision of the server too. The first response of a newer deploy informs BigPipe/newRevision as a state, with the revision and the one of the page, e.g. to offer to reload, and the next page transition loads the page in full, with the new scripts: new Arbiter().subscribe('BigPipe/newRevision', ({ revision }) => { showBanner('A new version is available.'); }); isOutdated() from bigpipe-util/dist/core/Revision tells it later.

A page that is left runs its leave hooks, its timers are cleared, and its requests in flight are abandoned unless they were sent with setAllowCrossPageTransition(true), see AsyncRequest: import PageTransitions from 'bigpipe-util/dist/PageTransitions'; import { setInterval } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/TimerStorage'; setInterval(refreshTimes, 60000); // cleared when the page is left PageTransitions.addBeforeLeaveHook(() => (form.dirty ? 'You have unsaved changes.' : null)); PageTransitions.addLeaveHook(() => player.stop()); Run registers the same hooks and works for full page loads too: Run.onBeforeUnload() and Run.onLeave(). core/TimerStorage has setTimeout, setInterval, requestAnimationFrame and requestIdleCallback (with their clear and cancel functions) that end with the page, and setTimeoutAcrossTransitions, setIntervalAcrossTransitions, requestAnimationFrameAcrossTransitions and requestIdleCallbackAcrossTransitions for the timers that outlive it. The plain browser functions outlive the page too.

Informed through Arbiter, exported as PAGE_TRANSITION_EVENT from PageTransitions and QUICKLING_EVENT from Quickling: Event When PageTransitions/beforeTransition Before a page is left, with from and to. PageTransitions/transition A handler loads the next page, with its uri. Quickling/unload The page is left for the next one. Quickling/send The request for the next page is sent. Quickling/firstResponse The response is about to be applied. Quickling/beforeClearCanvas The canvas is about to be emptied. Quickling/response The response was applied. PageTransitions/beforeFragmentTransition Before a fragment of the same page is scrolled to, with the from and to fragments. PageTransitions/fragmentTransition A link to a fragment of the page was followed, with its fragment. Handlers of other kinds of page transitions can be added with PageTransitions.registerHandler(handler, priority): a handler gets the URL and returns true when it loads the page.

A pagelet is an independent part of the page, like a sidebar or a feed, with its own content, CSS and JavaScript. BigPipe shows each pagelet as soon as its CSS is loaded and loads the JavaScript files of the pagelets only after all of them are displayed, so scripts never delay the content. The server renders the pagelets, see dobron\BigPipe\Pagelet in the PHP library. For every pagelet, it outputs: (window.__bigpipe = window.__bigpipe || []).push(['arrive', { id: "sidebar", css: ["/css/sidebar.css"], js: ["/js/sidebar.js"], domops: [["setContent", "#sidebar", false, {"__html": "..."}]], jsmods: {"require": [["Sidebar", "init", []]]}, onload: {"require": [["SidebarChat", "connect", []]]}, onafterload: {"require": [["SidebarPrefetch", "start", []]]}, is_last: true, }]); The script queues the pagelet until the entrypoint has run, so the entrypoint can be loaded any way, see Getting started.

Arrive. The CSS files of the pagelet start loading through the Bootloader, which loads every file once. Display. When its CSS (and its display resources) is loaded, the DOM operations of the pagelet are applied and its jsmods are handled by ServerJS. A module of the page bundle runs right away, a bootloadable module once its files are loaded. Load JS. When the last pagelet (is_last) has arrived and all pagelets are displayed, the JS files of all pagelets start loading. A pagelet with jsNonBlock loads its JS files right after it is displayed instead. Onload. When the JS files of a pagelet are loaded, its onload jsmods are handled: the module calls that need those files. Pagelets run their onload jsmods in the order they arrived. After load. When every pagelet has run its onload jsmods and the window has loaded, the optional onafterload jsmods of the pagelets are handled. Use them for work that must not compete with the page, like prefetching or analytics. The phases are exported as BIGPIPE_PHASE and PAGELET_PHASE from bigpipe-util/dist/BigPipe. BigPipe is a singleton, so new BigPipe() always returns the same instance with the registered pagelets.

Pagelets are displayed as soon as their CSS is loaded, in any order. The server can order them, see Pagelet::setPhase() and Pagelet::displayAfter() in the PHP library: phase (default 0): a pagelet is displayed after the pagelets of a lower phase that have arrived, e.g. the content of the page in phase 0 before the sidebar and ads in phase 1. The server sends the pagelets in the order of their phases. display_dependency: the ids of the pagelets it is displayed after, e.g. a chat that needs the feed on the page. It waits for them to arrive. (window.__bigpipe = window.__bigpipe || []).push(['arrive', { id: "chat", phase: 1, display_dependency: ["feed"], // ... }]); The JS of the pagelets still loads only when all of them are displayed.

Every pagelet informs Pagelet/event through Arbiter on each step of its lifecycle, with the event, the id of the pagelet and the time ts from performance.now(): Event When arrive The pagelet arrived. css Its CSS files start loading. cssLoad Its CSS files are loaded. displayStart Its DOM operations are about to be applied. display It is displayed. jsStart The JS files start loading. jsDone Its JS files are loaded, its jsmods run next. onload Its jsmods have run. The times are kept in pagelet.timings and marked with performance.mark() as pagelet_<id>_<event>, so they show in the performance panel of the browser. The names are exported as PAGELET_EVENT. The page informs its own events, exported as BIGPIPE_EVENT, with the time ts: BigPipe/init when BigPipe is created, BigPipe/tti when the time to interactive is reached, BigPipe/allPageletsDisplayed when the last pagelet has arrived and all are displayed, and BigPipe/allPageletsLoaded when all have run their jsmods. They are informed as states, so a module that subscribes later is called right away, and they are marked with performance.mark() as well. The pagelets of a response, e.g. a lazy pagelet, do not count for them: they load their JS on their own, once the last of them has arrived and all are displayed. The pagelets of a page transition are the next page, which informs them again. new Arbiter().subscribe('Pagelet/event', ({ event, id, ts }) => { if (event === 'display') { analytics.track('pagelet_displayed', { id, ts }); } });

With a nonce-based policy, BigPipe adds the nonce of the page to the stylesheets and scripts it loads. It takes the nonce from the CSPNonce module, which the PHP library defines in the page script after BigPipe::setNonce(), or else from the first <script nonce="..."> on the page, e.g. the inline script of the page. With Trusted Types, a policy that requires them (require-trusted-types-for 'script') blocks strings in innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, the src of a script and the Function constructor. BigPipe passes the HTML of the server, the scripts the Bootloader loads and the code of the deprecated eval DOM operation through its own policy, bigpipe, so allow it: Content-Security-Policy: require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types bigpipe The policy passes the values as they are: they come from the server of the page, like the page itself. Browsers without Trusted Types get the strings.

A pagelet can be loaded later from an endpoint, e.g. a pagelet below the fold. The server prints its placeholder, the root element of the pagelet, and calls UIPagelet.loadFromEndpoint() with it, see LazyPagelet in the PHP library: UIPagelet.loadFromEndpoint('/pagelets/feed', 'pagelet_feed', { page: 2 }, { load: 'visible' }); It requests the URL with the data when the placeholder comes within 300 pixels of the viewport (visible, default), when the browser is idle (idle) or right away (load). The response puts the pagelet in the place of the placeholder, and BigPipe loads its CSS and JS like on a page. While it loads, the placeholder has the async-saving class, and errors go to the default error handler. When the pagelet the placeholder is in is destroyed, it stops waiting and aborts the request.

A list loads its next page when the user scrolls to its end. The server prints a plain "See more" link handled by the Primer and creates MorePagerFetchOnScroll with it, see MorePager in the PHP library: new MorePagerFetchOnScroll(document.getElementById('more_pager'), 300); It clicks the link when it comes within the offset of the viewport. The response appends the items and replaces the link with the one of the next page, or removes it. remove() stops waiting, and so does destroying the pagelet the link is in.

The pagelets of the first phases are the content the user is waiting for, the others are the rest of the page. The server tells which ones with tti_phase, a field of a pagelet: the time to interactive is reached when every pagelet of the phases up to it is displayed. new Arbiter().subscribe('BigPipe/tti', ({ phase, ts }) => { analytics.track('interactive', { phase, ts }); }); The event is informed once per page as a state, so a module that subscribes later is called right away. It waits until no pagelet of the phases up to tti_phase can arrive any more: the server marked the last pagelet of the phase with last_in_phase, or a pagelet of a later phase or the last pagelet has arrived. A page transition forgets it for the next page.

The server marks the last pagelet of every phase with last_in_phase, so the browser knows a phase is complete without waiting for the next one, which may take longer to render. Once every pagelet of a phase and of the phases before it is displayed, BigPipe/phaseDisplayed is informed with the phase, e.g. to start what can wait for the first screen. It is informed once, not as a state, so a module that subscribes later is not called; new BigPipe().isPhaseDisplayed(phase) tells whether the phase is displayed already: new Arbiter().subscribe('BigPipe/phaseDisplayed', ({ phase }) => { if (phase === 0) { startChat(); } }); Without last_in_phase, a phase is complete once the last pagelet of the page has arrived. Right after the time to interactive, the browser downloads the js and allResources of the pagelets of the later phases in the background (<link rel="preload">), without running them. The scripts then are in the cache when the pagelets load their JS, after all of them are displayed, and nothing competes with the content of the first phases before. A pagelet of a later phase that arrives after the time to interactive is prefetched when it arrives.

A pagelet is destroyed when a pagelet with the same id replaces it, e.g. when the server refreshes it, or when the DOM operations of a response remove its root element. Destroying a pagelet destroys the pagelets inside it, runs its destructors, informs Pagelet/destroy with its id and root through Arbiter and empties its root element. A module stops what it started for a pagelet in a destructor, e.g. a subscription or a timer: import BigPipe from 'bigpipe-util/dist/BigPipe'; import Arbiter from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Arbiter'; export default class Feed { init(element) { const subscription = new Arbiter().subscribe('POST/ADDED', post => this.add(post)); const timer = setInterval(() => this.refreshTimes(), 60000); new BigPipe().getPageletForNode(element)?.addDestructor(() => { subscription.remove(); clearInterval(timer); }); } } getPageletForNode() finds the pagelet an element is in, by its root element #pagelet_<id>. getRoot() returns the root of a displayed pagelet, and removePagelet(pagelet) destroys a pagelet.

A failing pagelet does not stop the page. A pagelet that fails to arrive is reported, and the next pagelets arrive as usual. When the DOM operations of a pagelet fail, the error is reported, Pagelet/error is informed through Arbiter with its id and the error, and the pagelet still counts as displayed: its modules run and the JS of the page loads. Every module call is isolated too, see ServerJS. new Arbiter().subscribe('Pagelet/error', ({ id }) => { document.getElementById('pagelet_' + id).classList.add('pagelet-failed'); }); Errors are reported with reportError(): they are thrown asynchronously, so they reach window.onerror and the error tracking of the page without stopping BigPipe.

Poller sends a request again and again, e.g. to check for new notifications. The next request is sent an interval after the last one finished, so slow responses never pile up. Like any AsyncRequest, the DOM operations and modules of a response are applied. The server starts a poller with a module call, see Poller in the PHP library: new Poller({ uri: '/notifications/poll', data: { since: 1728550000 }, interval: 30000 }); Option Default Description uri, method, data GET The request to send. Without uri, setupRequest sets up the request. setupRequest (request, poller) => …, sets up every request, e.g. its handler. interval Milliseconds between two requests, at least 2 seconds, or a function of the number of requests. maxRequests no limit The poller stops after this many requests and informs done. muteWhenHidden true Pauses while the page is hidden, e.g. in a background tab. muteWhenIdle 0 Pauses when the user was not active for this many milliseconds, and goes on once they are. clearOnQuicklingEvents true A page transition ends the poller. dontStart false Waits for start(). id Lets the server control the poller, see below. A poller is controlled with start(), stop(), reset(), mute(), resume(), skip() (skips the next request), setInterval(ms) and destroy(). subscribe('done', callback) is called when it stops after maxRequests.

With an id, every request of the poller sends the __poller parameter with it, and a response can call the methods of the poller as the module of that id, e.g. to poll less often or to stop: {"jsmods": {"require": [["poller_notifications", "setInterval", [60000]]]}}

The poller uses two modules that can be used on their own: core/Visibility: isHidden(), and subscribe(Visibility.HIDDEN | Visibility.VISIBLE, callback) when the page is hidden or shown. It informs Visibility/hidden and Visibility/visible through Arbiter, with the changeTime. core/UserActivity: isActive(ms), whether the user scrolled, moved the mouse, clicked, typed or focused the window in the last ms milliseconds, and subscribe(callback) when they are active again after more than half a second. It informs UserActivity/activity through Arbiter, with the DOM event, the idleness in milliseconds and the time of the inform, lastInform.

The Primer makes links and forms asynchronous without writing any JavaScript. It registers a single click and submit listener on the document, so it also works for content added later. import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; Primer(); The Primer cancels the click or submit at once and sends the request through AsyncRequest as soon as it is available, so it can be started early and AsyncRequest loaded on demand, see Loading AsyncRequest on demand.

Add the URL to call in ajaxify, or in href when the link has no ajaxify, and pick the behaviour with rel: Remove item rel Method Description async GET Sends the request and handles the response. async-post POST The same as async, but with POST. dialog POST Intended for requests that open a dialog. Links with a real href (other than #) still open normally when clicked with the middle mouse button or with a modifier key, so users can open them in a new tab.

Forms with rel="async" are submitted in the background. The form data, including the name and value of the button that submitted it, is sent to ajaxify or, if missing, to action, with the form's method. <form action="/ajax/subscribe.php" method="POST" rel="async"> <input name="email" type="email"> <button type="submit" name="plan" value="free">Subscribe</button> </form> While the request is running: the inputs, selects and textareas are made read-only and the submit button is disabled, unless the form has the disable-prevent-form class, an element with the form-loader class inside the form gets the loading class.

A form with rel="async" and a chosen file is sent as multipart/form-data, so PHP reads the files from $_FILES. While the data is uploaded the form reports the progress, three ways, so use what suits your markup: <form action="/upload.php" method="POST" rel="async"> <input type="file" name="photo"> <progress></progress> <!-- value and max are set, and reset when the request is over --> <button type="submit">Upload</button> </form> form.addEventListener('uploadprogress', ({ detail }) => { console.log(detail.loaded, detail.total, detail.ratio); // bubbles from the form }); form::after { content: ''; display: block; height: 4px; background: currentColor; transform: scaleX(var(--upload-progress, 0)); /* the ratio from 0 to 1 while uploading */ transform-origin: left; } Only a form with a chosen file reports progress. For your own requests use AsyncRequest.setUploadProgressHandler().

The Primer does not import AsyncRequest: it asks the Bootloader for the module bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest, which the module loader resolves like the modules the server calls (the ModuleRegistry of this package provides it). A click before the module is available is not lost and does not follow the link: it is cancelled and the request is sent the moment the module is loaded. Further clicks on the same link, or submits of the same form, are ignored in the meantime, and the data of a form is the data at the time of the submit. This lets a small entrypoint with the Primer run early, e.g. in the <head>, while AsyncRequest and the rest of the library load later: early.js import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; import Bootloader from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Bootloader'; Bootloader.setResourceMap({ 'main.js': { type: 'js', src: '/static/main.js' } }); Bootloader.enableBootload({ 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest': ['main.js'] }); Primer(); main.js is the entrypoint with import 'bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry'; once it has run, the module resolves and the waiting requests are sent. If the module can't be loaded, the error is reported and the link or form works again.

The link or form gets the async-saving class while its request is running. Clicks on a link with this class are ignored, which prevents double submits. Use it to show a spinner: .async-saving { cursor: progress; opacity: 0.6; }
The requests of links and forms have no error handler of their own, so their errors go to the default error handler, e.g. to show them in a dialog.
The link or form becomes the relative element of the request. DOM operations with an empty selector target it, see DOM operations.

Run registers callbacks for the moments of a page's life: when it is loaded, before it is left and when it is left. They work for a full page load and for a page transition alike, so the same code is right whether the user closes the tab or follows a link that loads the next page into the canvas. Every function returns a subscription, remove() unregisters the callback, and an error in a callback is reported without stopping the others. import Run from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Run'; Run.onLoad(() => init()); // the DOM is ready Run.onAfterLoad(() => prefetch()); // the window has loaded Run.onBeforeUnload(() => (dirty ? 'You have unsaved changes.' : null)); Run.onLeave(() => socket.close()); // the page is left Run.onUnload(() => navigator.sendBeacon('/log', data)); Run.onCleanupOrLeave(element, () => observer.disconnect()); Function Runs onLoad(callback) When the DOM is ready, or right away if it already is. onAfterLoad(callback) After the load event of the window, or on the next tick if it already happened. onBeforeUnload(hook) Before the page is left. The hook returns a message to ask the user first, or nothing. onLeave(callback) Once, when the page is left with a page transition, closed, reloaded or navigated away from. onUnload(callback) When the page is closed, reloaded or navigated away from (pagehide), not on a page transition. onCleanupOrLeave(element, callback) Once, when the pagelet or canvas that holds the element is destroyed, or the page is left.

onBeforeUnload() asks for confirmation before the user loses unsaved work. For a page transition the message is shown with confirm() and declining keeps the page; for a close or a reload the browser shows its own prompt, with its own text. When a page transition ends in a full page load because no handler loads the page, the user is asked once. onLeave() is the place to stop what the page started: sockets, observers, listeners on the document. Use onUnload() only for what must run when the page really goes away, like sending a beacon, as a page transition keeps the document. A page the browser keeps in its back/forward cache (pagehide with persisted) can come back as it was with the back button, so neither onLeave() nor onUnload() runs then. A cached page that is later dropped from the cache gets no event at all, so send what must not be lost, like analytics, when the page is hidden (visibilitychange) rather than in onUnload(). FormMonitor uses onBeforeUnload() to ask before a form with unsaved changes is left. onCleanupOrLeave() ties a cleanup to an element. The elements inside a pagelet are gone when the pagelet is destroyed, e.g. when a page transition empties the canvas or a response replaces the pagelet, long before the page is left: class Clock { init(element) { const timer = setInterval(() => (element.textContent = new Date().toLocaleTimeString()), 1000); Run.onCleanupOrLeave(element, () => clearInterval(timer)); } } The timers of core/TimerStorage and the requests of a page end with it without any of this, see Page transitions.

ServerJS calls the JavaScript modules that the server requires. It handles the jsmods of every response and, at the end of the page, the modules required while rendering it. BigPipe::render() in the PHP library prints them in an inline script that queues them until the entrypoint has run, see Getting started: (window.__bigpipe = window.__bigpipe || []).push(['handle', jsmods]);

jsmods.require is a list of [module, method, args]: { "require": [ ["UserLoggedInAlert", null, ["Marvin"]], ["ChartRenderer", "render", [{"__e": "chart"}, [10, 20, 30]]] ] } The module is resolved by the loader set with setModuleLoader(), see Getting started. Without a method, the module is called as a constructor with the arguments: new UserLoggedInAlert('Marvin'). An instance is only created, if it was not yet. With a method, a class is instantiated without arguments and the method is called with them: new ChartRenderer().render(element, [10, 20, 30]). A module that exports an object has the method called on the object directly. In PHP: $response->bigPipe()->require("require('UserLoggedInAlert')", ['Marvin']); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('ChartRenderer').render()", [ \dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker::element('chart'), [10, 20, 30], ]);

A call with a method creates a new object of a class every time. To keep one object and talk to it from more calls, the server defines an instance in jsmods.instances, a list of [id, module, args]: { "instances": [["__inst_u_0_1", "ChartRenderer", [{"__e": "chart"}, [10, 20, 30]]]], "require": [ ["__inst_u_0_1", "render"], ["Dashboard", "add", [{"__m": "__inst_u_0_1"}]] ] } The instance is created with new ChartRenderer(element, [10, 20, 30]) the first time something requires it, by its id in require or in a __m transport marker, and every later use gets the same object, also in the following responses. In PHP: $chart = $response->bigPipe()->instance('ChartRenderer', [ \dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker::element('chart'), [10, 20, 30], ]); $chart->call('render'); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('Dashboard').add()", [$chart]);

The server can send data as a module, e.g. the configuration of the page or the current user, in jsmods.define, a list of [name, exports]: { "define": [["SiteData", {"locale": "sk_SK", "user": {"id": 7}}]] } The module is required like any other, requireModule('SiteData'), or passed to a call with a __m transport marker. Its transport markers are replaced when it is required for the first time. Defines are handled before the instances and calls of the same jsmods, and a module defined again, e.g. by a later response, replaces the previous one. In PHP: $response->bigPipe()->define('SiteData', [ 'locale' => 'sk_SK', 'user' => ['id' => 7], ]);

A module can stand for another one that the server chooses, e.g. the variant of a feature flag or an A/B test for the user, or null to turn a feature off. The define is {"__rc": module}: { "define": [["Editor", {"__rc": "EditorNext"}], ["Chat", {"__rc": null}]] } The JavaScript does not know which one it gets: requireModule('Editor'), requireLazy(['Editor'], ...), a call of Editor and a {"__m": "Editor"} marker get EditorNext. When EditorNext is bootloadable, only its resources are loaded, so the page never downloads the variants it does not use. A module turned off is null: its calls do nothing, and ifRequired('Chat', ...) calls back the function for a missing module. requireLazy(['Editor'], Editor => Editor.open(textarea)); ifRequired('Chat', Chat => Chat.mount()); In PHP: $response->bigPipe()->defineCond('Editor', $user->isBeta() ? 'EditorNext' : 'EditorClassic'); $response->bigPipe()->defineCond('Chat', $chatEnabled ? 'ChatDock' : null);

Every define, instance and call runs on its own: when one fails, e.g. a module that doesn't exist or a method that throws, the others still run and the pagelet still finishes. The error is thrown again asynchronously, so it shows in the console and reaches window.onerror and error trackers.

Arguments are JSON, so values that JSON can't express are sent as markers and replaced before the module is called: Marker Replaced with PHP __e The element with this id. TransportMarker::element() __m The module, resolved the same way as require. TransportMarker::module() __rel The element that sent the request, e.g. the link of the Primer, or null. TransportMarker::relative() __map A Map created from the list of [key, value]. TransportMarker::map() __set A Set created from the list of values. TransportMarker::set() __html Used for the HTML content of DOM operations; a module gets the object. TransportMarker::html() Markers are replaced at any depth of the arguments. handle(jsmods, relativeTo) takes the element of __rel; AsyncResponse passes the relative element of the request.

Calls the callback after the load event of the window, or on the next tick if the page is already loaded. import onAfterLoad from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/onAfterLoad'; onAfterLoad(() => console.log('The page is loaded.')); See Run for removable subscriptions and the hooks for leaving a page.

Calls the callback once, when the element comes within buffer pixels of the viewport, e.g. to load content right before the user scrolls to it. remove() of the returned subscription stops waiting. import onVisible from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/onVisible'; const subscription = onVisible(element, () => console.log('Almost visible.'), { buffer: 300 });
import ReloadPage from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ReloadPage'; new ReloadPage().now(); new ReloadPage().delay(250); // in ms The server calls it with $response->reload($delay).

import ServerRedirect from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ServerRedirect'; new ServerRedirect().redirectPageTo('/onboarding', 500); // delay in ms new ServerRedirect().redirectPageTo('/feed', 0, true, true); // replace the history entry, page transition It loads the URL in full, or with transition with a page transition when the page has them on. replace replaces the current history entry, e.g. of a form that should not be sent again with the back button. A redirect with a delay does not happen once the page is left with a page transition. The server calls it with $response->redirect($url, $delay, $replace, $transition).

Keeps data for an element, any other object or a string namespace, without putting it on the element. The data of an element goes away with the element. import DataStore from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/DataStore'; DataStore.set(button, 'tooltip', tooltip); DataStore.get(button, 'tooltip'); DataStore.get(button, 'count', 0); // the data-count attribute of the element, or else 0 DataStore.remove(button, 'tooltip'); DataStore.purge(button); // removes all data of the element

Sets the title of the page and lets it blink, e.g. to show a new message in a background tab. Page transitions set the title with it too. import DocumentTitle from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/DocumentTitle'; DocumentTitle.set('Messages'); // informs DocumentTitle/update DocumentTitle.set('(2) Messages', true); // a temporary title, get() still returns 'Messages' const blinking = DocumentTitle.blink('New message'); // alternates every 1.5 seconds blinking.stop();

Keyboard shortcuts. A key is a name of KeyEventController.KEYS (ESCAPE, RETURN, SLASH, UP, ...) or a character. By default, a shortcut runs on keydown without Ctrl, Alt or Meta, and not while the user types in a text field, except navigation keys like ESCAPE in an empty one. A callback that returns false prevents the default action and stops the other shortcuts of the key. import KeyEventController from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/KeyEventController'; KeyEventController.registerKey('j', () => feed.next()); KeyEventController.registerKey('SLASH', () => { search.focus(); return false; }); const subscription = KeyEventController.registerKeyAcrossTransitions('ESCAPE', () => dialog.hide()); subscription.remove(); A page transition removes the shortcuts of the page; the ones registered across transitions stay. registerKey(key, callback, filter, replace) takes another filter (event, type) => boolean, and with replace it replaces the other shortcuts of the key.

The local and session storage, or null when the browser does not allow them, e.g. in a private window, and reads and writes that never throw. import WebStorage from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/WebStorage'; const storage = WebStorage.getLocalStorage(); // or getSessionStorage() const error = WebStorage.setItemGuarded(storage, 'draft', text); // null, or the error, e.g. a full storage const draft = WebStorage.getItemGuarded(storage, 'draft'); // null without the storage WebStorage.removeItemGuarded(storage, 'draft');

Reads and writes cookies. A cookie is set for the path / with SameSite=Lax, and Secure on HTTPS. import Cookie from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Cookie'; Cookie.set('theme', 'dark', { lifetime: 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 }); // milliseconds, a session cookie without it Cookie.get('theme'); // 'dark', or null Cookie.clear('theme'); set() also takes path, domain, secure and sameSite, and clear() takes path and domain.
